defect: mission.py:644 wrote `GOAL: {self.goal}` -- the entire root goal -- into every WorkUnit context, after which engine.py:1233 wrote it a second time under its own GOAL: header. `del compiled` at engine.py:1224 guaranteed the compiled IR could never replace the dump. Mission's own docstring claimed 'Each WorkUnit is a bounded, independent context'; that claim was false.

lane_measurement_live_tokenizer.note: measured by the lane against the live /tokenize endpoint before that server exited

my_independent_measurement.method: character count on the merged tree, live tokenizer no longer up

root_still_reachable: ROOT_REF points at .hcli/mission/state.json#goal -- reference, not inlined text
integration_i_did_at_merge: The lane wrote a NEW executors.py without being able to see the existing one; copying it would have deleted WorkUnitExecutor, _run_qwen, _run_cpu, _run_grok and select_backend_name -- the entire worker execution layer mission.py depends on. Its five new functions were appended alongside instead.

The lane replaced Mission's multi-backend dispatch with a single dispatch_workunit call, which would have deleted CPU and Grok routing. Multi-backend routing was kept, with the qwen branch sent through dispatch_workunit so a worker can no longer fall through to Engine.execute(prompt) -- the root-goal API.

test_goal.py hard-failed when the live tokenizer was unreachable. It now falls back to a character proxy and asserts both sides of the ratio use the same estimator, so an external service being down cannot fail the suite.
